medical-reference-document.title: WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care: Acute Coronary and Resuscitation Protocols

section.title: WHO Acute Coronary Resuscitation - MONA Protocol and Early Defibrillation

sections.section: In patients presenting with suspected acute coronary syndrome or myocardial infarction, initial emergency management comprises: 1. Immediate resting 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) performed and interpreted within 10 minutes of arrival. 2. Oxygen supplementation only if hypoxemic (SpO2 < 90%). 3. Immediate chewable Aspirin (162-325 mg) unless contraindicated by active hemorrhage. 4. Sublingual nitroglycerin (0.4 mg every 5 minutes up to 3 doses) for ischemic chest discomfort, provided SBP is > 90 mmHg and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors have not been taken in past 24-48 hours. 5. Rapid cardiac biomarker assessment (high-sensitivity cardiac troponin). 6. For ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia cardiac arrest, immediate cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and rapid automated external defibrillation (AED) are the determinative survival factors.
